introduction.text: Two giant impacts carved Vesta's Rheasilvia and Veneneia basins and the troughs that circle it.

normal.title: FC natural-color composite
normal.summary: The 650, 550 and 430 nm bands approximate visible color; beyond its coverage the HAMO mosaic shows in gray.

ratios.title: Clementine-style color composite
ratios.summary: Published false-color filter ratios that emphasize spectral differences.

elevation.title: HAMO digital terrain model
elevation.summary: Height above or below a 255 km sphere; polar gaps are interpolated.

surface.title: LAMO clear-filter mosaic
surface.summary: Low-altitude photographs of crater walls and troughs; the north LAMO never saw takes the HAMO mosaic in gray.

hamo.title: HAMO clear-filter mosaic
hamo.summary: High-altitude photographs of the whole surface, north pole included under low sun; illumination and seams remain.

hydrogen.title: GRaND hydrogen
hydrogen.summary: Hydrogen in the top decimetres, richest where dark carbon-rich material fell; each value blends about 300 km.

iron.title: GRaND iron gamma rays
iron.summary: Iron gamma-ray rate: basaltic eucrite reads higher than Rheasilvia's diogenite; each value blends about 300 km.

fast-neutrons.title: GRaND fast neutrons
fast-neutrons.summary: Fast neutrons, hydrogen trend removed, follow average atomic mass: heavier eucrite reads higher; each blends about 300 km.

hegr.title: GRaND high-energy gamma rays
hegr.summary: High-energy gamma rays rise with heavy major elements: eucrite over Rheasilvia's diogenite; each value blends about 300 km.

neutron-absorption.title: GRaND neutron absorption
neutron-absorption.summary: How strongly the soil absorbs slow neutrons: high where basaltic eucrite is, low in Rheasilvia; each blends about 300 km.

geology.title: Yingst et al. global geologic map
geology.summary: Interpreted rock units: crater floors, ejecta, cratered terrain and Rheasilvia's flanks, in the authors' colors.

gravity.title: VESTA20H radial gravity
gravity.summary: How strongly Vesta pulls at each place, with its overall flattening removed. Red pulls harder, blue weaker.

gravity-uncertainty.title: VESTA20H gravity uncertainty
gravity-uncertainty.summary: How far the gravity map may be off at each place. It is least certain toward the south pole.

bouguer.title: VESTA20H Bouguer anomaly, degree 15
bouguer.summary: Gravity left after removing the pull of the visible shape. Red marks denser rock underground.

geoid.title: VESTA20H geoid height
geoid.summary: Height of the surface where a global ocean would settle. Shown within 60° of the equator, where it is valid.
